title: Mosaic feedback scratchpad and risked probes - 2026-01-14
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
This scratchpad captures a set of clustered customer signals gathered in Q4 2025–Q1 2026, along with experimentally-oriented probe ideas ("risked probes") we can run quickly to validate tradeoffs. The intent is pragmatic: surface low-code, low-cost experiments that resolve key unresolved hypotheses for product, runtime, and SRE teams.

Topline themes (raw synthesis):
- Latency sensitivity vs cost: multiple customers (adtech, search SaaS, and a mid-market document automation vendor) report brittle UX when latency varies; they are willing to trade small quality/throughput for lower p99 tails.
- Caching confusion & safety: customers ask for clearer guarantees/documentation around prefix/KV cache semantics (staleness, invalidation triggers) — several reported surprising outputs after model rollouts.
- Private deployment onboarding friction: security review and network config repeatedly block pilot launches; customers want a checklist and a test harness for common corporate firewall patterns.
- Model fallback observability: operators want stronger visibility when fallback routing to cheaper/quantized variants happens and an easy opt-in to automatic fallback for specific customer routes.
- Embeddings consistency: a few customers noticed subtle drift in embeddings between model versions and quantization profiles affecting downstream similarity search.

Representative vignettes (anonymized):
1) Search startup (early-stage, bursty traffic): p99 spike during a holiday campaign caused a 2x surge in API errors; they disabled streaming and accepted slower completion to reduce failures. Outcome: temporarily degraded UX and churn risk.
2) Healthcare integration partner (on Private): security team required IP allowlist + internal proxy; customer spent 2 weeks looping in infra vendor before a pilot started. Outcome: long time-to-value, lost momentum.
3) Enterprise legal SaaS: after a model rollout to a quantized variant, similarity ranking for clause-matching regressed by 3% on their eval set. They didn't get notified because alert rules were lax. Outcome: rollback + blame on ambiguity of rollout notes.

Signal clusters (why these matter):
- Latency-cost tradeoffs: customers want a tunable knob that maps directly to expected p50/p95/p99 and $/1M tokens — not just an opaque 'quantization' toggle.
- Cache semantics & rollout coupling: KV prefix cache + model variant rollouts interact in surprising ways; lack of automatic invalidation stories causes stale behavior.
- Private onboarding patterns: repeated network proxies and KMS/HSM policies mean we need templated reference architectures per major cloud or common enterprise proxy setups.

Risked probes (short experiments; prioritized):
1) Micro-SLO toggle A/B probe (effort: M, risk: low)
- Hypothesis: exposing an "SLO profile" (latency-targeted | cost-targeted | balanced) will let customers choose predictable p99 cost/latency behavior and reduce friction in SLA conversations.
- Success metric: 30% of pilot customers choose a non-default profile and p99 tail incidents drop by 25% for those routes in 4 weeks.
- Implementation sketch: add route-level profile flag in account settings; runtime maps flags to batching thresholds, max latency queue time, and model-variant preference. Instrument p50/p95/p99.
- Owner(s): product-hosted-api + serving-runtime.

2) Cache-invalidation safety shim (effort: S, risk: medium)
- Hypothesis: a lightweight explicit "cache-bust" API and a per-route cache-age header will stop most stale-output reports and reduce rollback incidents.
- Success metric: reduce reported "stale output" tickets by 50% in 2 months in pilot group.
- Implementation sketch: add admin POST /routes/:id/cache-bust, add X-Cache-Generation header on responses, document semantics. Optional: a warning when a rollout changes model family without automatic cache migration.
- Owner(s): platform-engineering + console-and-rollouts.

3) Private deployment quickstart harness (effort: M, risk: low)
- Hypothesis: provide an enterprise networking quickstart (Terraform + test harness scripts + curl tests) will cut Private onboarding time by >= 50%.
- Success metric: median onboarding time for pilots drops from ~14 days to <=7 days.
- Implementation sketch: maintain per-cloud repo with example NACLs, proxy sidecar config, and a smoke-test container that exercises API and KMS handshake. Add explicit docs checklist.
- Owner(s): private-deployments + solutions-engineering-and-professional-services.

4) Quantization consistency audit and embedding baseline (effort: L, risk: medium-high)
- Hypothesis: a defined embedding compatibility test suite and a quantized-quality baseline will surface regressions before rollouts and reduce post-rollout complaints.
- Success metric: 90% of embedding regressions detected in CI before customer-facing rollout for pilot customers.
- Implementation sketch: create a shared "embedding-canonical" dataset with typical customer queries, run end-to-end pipeline on every quantized build, fail rollouts on >1.5% drift on chosen metric.
- Owner(s): applied-ml + serving-runtime + product-optimize.

Quick wins and playbacks (immediately actionable):
- Create a one-page "Private deployment checklist" for sales + solutions to share during contract negotiation (owner: solutions-engineering).
- Add a short wording change to rollout email templates: include "expected cache impact" field to surface potential stale behavior. (owner: console-and-rollouts).
- Triage a small internal postmortem template for p99 spike incidents that asks "did model variant change?" and "was cache invalidation performed?" (owner: site-reliability-engineering).

Unresolved questions / decision points:
- How opinionated should SLO profiles be? Conservative mapping reduces customer surprise but might limit sophisticated customers. We need a default that protects p99.
- Is global cache generation enough, or do we need per-customer/per-model cache tags? Tradeoff: complexity vs safety.
- For embedding baseline, what is the canonical dataset? Must balance representativeness (customers across verticals) vs feasibility (size).

Suggested next steps (30/60/90):
- 30d: Ship Private deployment one-pager + quickstart repo skeleton; add rollout-email cache-impact field; start a pilot for cache-bust API with 2 customers.
- 60d: Implement route SLO-profile prototype in staging and run internal load-tests; finalize cache-bust semantics; draft embedding baseline proposal.
- 90d: Run embedding compatibility CI on a small set of quantized builds; iterate SLO-profile mapping using pilot customer feedback; measure onboarding time change for Private.

Notes, references, and quick links:
- Slack threads: #cs-runtime-threads (see Jan 2026 thread: "p99 tail during sales demo")
- Jira: JIRA-4621 (customer ticket with failed pilot due to proxy), JIRA-4700 (embedding regression report)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/pr/1189 (initial cache-bust endpoint sketch)

Action items (assigned):
- Aisha: compile pilot customers list for SLO-profile trial and reach out to two search/SaaS contacts (due: 2026-01-21).
- Evan: prototype minimal X-Cache-Generation header in staging and add instrumentation (due: 2026-02-05).
- Priya: draft Private quickstart checklist and repo README; coordinate with solutions-engineering (due: 2026-01-28).
- Liam: scope embedding baseline dataset and propose candidate corpora (due: 2026-02-12).

Appendix — short glossary for stakeholders:
- Cache-bust: explicit operation to increment route-level cache generation and signal clients that cached KV/prefix entries are stale.
- SLO-profile: a user-selectable route-level preset that adjusts batching, max batch wait, and preferred model variant order to hit latency or cost targets.
- Embedding baseline: a small canonical dataset + metrics suite used to detect vector-space drift across model/quantization changes.

This doc is a working scratchpad; expecting iterative edits. Use linked artifacts above for deeper context. If you want a condensed one-pager for execs, I can produce a 1-page brief that highlights metrics, cost impact estimation, and recommended first experiment.
